changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7125-dashboard-empty-state-keys-retired.md`

- names `DatasetWidget.tsx` → `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DatasetWidget.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `table.noRows` (`'No rows to display'`) and `engine.form.noRows` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, read at `widgets.tsx`) — two different, same-named keys in different namespaces. Nor the comments in `WidgetEmptyState.tsx`, `DatasetWidget.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and `PivotTable.tsx` that record WHY three widgets with three strings became one shared empty state; the packs' own comment keeps that rationale and now names the retirement instead of a row that is gone.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `e420df310` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1850 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2462 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36784961156)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7d54b7cfbe5042569dac72c80409314b34e0dc0a`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read, and nothing else: card #11261 (body and all 3 comments: triage `5918660676`, claim `5919807834`, os-dev-report `5920760284`); PR #11278 (body, 4-file list, the three-dot diff against `main`; merge base `f61dab169`, 2 commits ahead, 8 behind); the head's check-runs with `filter=latest`; objectui#8894's retriage answer `5918678067` as context for item 5. Files read at the head for context (REST `contents`, no checkout): `DatasetWidget.tsx`, the three test files this diff names (`dimensionlessMeasures-11261`, `unrenderedMeasures-8894`, `subCaption`), `packages/react/src/hooks/useDatasetDimensionLabels.ts`, `packages/plugin-dashboard/package.json`, and the six dashboard docs (`content/docs/blocks/dashboard.mdx`, `fields/widget-props.mdx`, `guide/dashboard-filters.md`, `plugins/plugin-dashboard.mdx`, the package README and SKILL). The stale local clone at `/home/user/objectui` (`0eb9f36ac`, which does not contain the merge base) was consulted for its ref only and nothing was read from it. Binding direction: triage `5918660676` items 1–5.

**Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts):** 43 latest runs, all completed at 22:36Z after a 4-minute foreground wait: 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`Test (coverage)`, the coverage shard matrix, `dependabot`), 0 failures. Every derived family is green: `Test` (8 shards, dist pins), `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Changeset Declaration` / `Bump Policy` / `Claim Re-read` / `Fixed Group Check` / `Overwrite Report`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Inert vi.mock Specifier Check`, the doc checks and the skill checks. The dev's local gate numbers (155 files / 1420 passed, type-check 0, eslint 0 errors, changeset-presence 0, control-bytes 0, citations 0, scripts suite 5371) are the dev's claims; the check-runs confirm each family at this head.

### ① Derived judgments

Item 1 — the classification (`DatasetWidget.tsx:493-494`). RIGHT. `rendersEveryMeasureWithoutDimension = values.length above 1 AND (isTable OR MEASURE_AXIS_CHART_FAMILIES.has(CHART_TYPE_MAP[widgetType] ?? ''))`, and `isMetric = METRIC_TYPES.has(type) OR (dimensions.length === 0 AND NOT that)`. Read against `CHART_TYPE_MAP` at the head, the types that leave the tile branch when dimensionless with 2+ measures are exactly: `table`, `pivot` (by `isTable`), and the CHART_TYPE_MAP members that resolve to the four named families: `bar`, `grouped-bar`, `stacked-bar`, `bi-polar-bar` (family `bar`); `line`, `spline`, `step-line` (family `line`); `area`, `stacked-area` (family `area`); `combo`. Not wider: `column` maps to `column` and `horizontal-bar` to `horizontal-bar` in `CHART_TYPE_MAP`, neither is in the set, so both still take the tile branch, as do `pie` / `donut` / `funnel` / `pyramid` / `scatter` / `bubble` / `radar` / `treemap` / `sankey`, an unknown type, and a typeless widget (`CHART_TYPE_MAP['']` is undefined, so the `?? ''` misses the set; the `chartType` line's `?? 'bar'` default is not consulted here, which is right). `METRIC_TYPES` is untouched, so the metric family is a tile by type, with or without dimensions. Coverage note, no action: the six family aliases (`grouped-bar`, `stacked-bar`, `bi-polar-bar`, `spline`, `step-line`, `stacked-area`) leave the tile through the same expression and are pinned by no row; the four canonical members are.

Item 1 — the transposition (`DatasetWidget.tsx:1712-1728`). RIGHT. `measuresOnAxis = dimensions.length === 0` is reachable only past the `isMetric` and `isTable` returns, so only a bar / line / area / combo family with 2+ measures reaches it (a dimensionless widget that is not one of those was returned as a tile above). It builds one row per declared measure in declaration order: category `headerLabel(m)` under the private key `__measure`, value `state.rows[0]?.[m]` under `__value` — the same `rows[0]` the tile reads, the `[]` grouping the dimensionless query answers. The single series is `{ dataKey: '__value', label: tt('dashboard.total', 'Total') }`: `dashboard.total` is the key the flat table's footer already reads at line 1554, so no locale key is minted, and the label is the grouping the row is. The two private keys cannot collide with a measure name because a transposed row carries only those keys. Overlay: a compared measure's `measure__compare` value rides under `__value__compare`; `comparedSeries` on this path is the one transposed series (when any measure compared), and the overlay takes `compareColumn('__value')` with the primary's mark and axis. The dimensioned path is byte-identical: `comparedSeries = comparedValues.map(m to { dataKey: m, label: headerLabel(m) })` feeds the same `dataKey` / label pair the old inline map produced. Pinned: bar and combo draw 2 `.recharts-bar-rectangle` with ticks `Revenue`, `Cost`; line / area plot across the two labels; the compare row draws 4 marks. Observations, no action: authored `chartConfig.series` entries keyed by a measure name bind to nothing on this path (the one derived series is keyed `__value`), which is what they bound to on the tile they replaced, so nothing regresses; and `canDrill` is false here (`drillDims` is empty and no `drillRanges` come back for a dimensionless query), so no drill semantics are added on the transposed chart or the one-row table.

Item 1 — the flat-table branch. RIGHT. `wantsFlatTotals = isTable AND NOT isMatrix AND dimensions.length above 0 AND limit == null` is a context line (unchanged at the head), so a dimensionless `table` / `pivot` asks the executor for no `totals` grouping and draws no footer; `isMatrix` needs 2 dimensions, so `pivot` takes the flat table. One row, its `td` cells the measures, its `th` cells the measure headers. Right for a row that IS the grand total: a `[]` grouping under a `[]` selection would print the same row twice, and the `colSpan={dimensions.length}` footer cell would be a zero span; the footer's comment was re-grounded on `wantsFlatTotals` rather than on "a zero-dimension widget returns above", which is now the true reason. Pinned for `table` and `pivot`: one `tbody` row `510000 / 120000 / 390000`, headers `revenue / cost / margin`, no `dataset-table-total-row`, no objectui#8894 warning.

Item 2 — one measure and no dimension. RIGHT. With `values.length` of 1 the new conjunct is false and `isMetric` collapses to `METRIC_TYPES.has(type) OR dimensions.length === 0`, the old expression, for every type. Pinned byte-identical (`REVENUE_TILE`) for `table`, `pivot`, `bar`, `line`, `area`, `combo`.

Item 4 — the query. RIGHT. `queryDataset(dataset, { dimensions, measures: values, ... })` is untouched; `totalsGroupings` is undefined for the dimensionless table (above); `compareTo` forwards for a bar family exactly as it did for the tile it was (`chartTypeIgnoresCompareTo('bar')` is false). Pinned: a dimensionless `table` and `bar` each query exactly `{ dimensions: [], measures: values }`. `useDatasetDimensionMeta` is now enabled for these widgets, but it returns before any read when `dims.length === 0` (`useDatasetDimensionLabels.ts:134`), so no object-schema read is added.

Item 4 — the ablation leg, against what the new file pins. CONSISTENT. The new file holds 25 rows: 7 SUBJECT (table + pivot via `it.each`, bar, combo, line + area via `it.each`, the compare overlay) and 18 CONTROL (the metric tile, six one-measure types, two query rows, nine unnamed types). Each SUBJECT asserts something the old `isMetric` makes false (a tile has no `tbody` row and draws no Recharts mark), and each CONTROL is green on both sides by construction. The dev's WRAP-mode ablation reports 7 failed / 38 passed over 45 rows: 25 + the 8894 file's 8 + the sub-caption file's 12 = 45, and 18 + 8 + 12 = 38, so the totals and the red set are consistent with the files at this head. PR objectui#8887's two pins (`subCaption.test.tsx` lines 107 and 178) are both on `type: 'metric'`, which `METRIC_TYPES` keeps a tile, so they stay green through this change; the head's `Test` shards confirm. The ablation itself is the dev's run and was not re-run here.

Item 3 — the nine CONTROL rows for the unnamed types. RIGHT. Each asserts the measured state (the `REVENUE_TILE` markup and the warning naming `"cost"`) under a title reading `measured, open question`, with a comment that the maintainer's answer is EXPECTED to change the row. They pin behaviour and assert no semantics; the display semantics are returned as Q1, as item 3 ordered.

No accept set or public type moves. RIGHT. The diff touches `DatasetWidget.tsx` (module-private `const` additions, no export change), one new test, one changed test example, and one changeset; no schema, no `packages/types`, no door. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and the changeset checks are green. The header docblock and the inline comments now state the new rule; no other in-file comment states the old one (line 519's "a pie widget with no dimensions renders as a metric tile" is still true).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11261-dimensionless-measures-render.md`: `'@object-ui/plugin-dashboard': patch` (the package's name at the head, version 17.6.0). RIGHT. The diff delivers a rendering the installed spec already states for widgets every door already accepts, and moves no API surface: patch. The changeset text names the spec sentence, the two arms, the unchanged one-measure case, the nine unnamed types and the unchanged query, which is what the diff publishes. `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy` and `Changeset Claim Re-read` are green.

Clause-②: no. RIGHT, and consistent: the claim `5919807834` says `Clause-②: no`, the PR body's second line says `Clause-②: no`, and the diff moves no schema, published type or accepted set.

### ③ Boundary flags

Deviation, the objectui#8894 file: one SUBJECT ("covers the dimensionless arm") moved from a dimensionless `bar` to a dimensionless `pie`, with its assertion (`measureWarning()` contains `"cost"`) unchanged and the warning code (`DatasetWidget.tsx:766-776`) untouched by any hunk. The file's intent survives: the row exists to prove the signal is keyed off the drop and not off the type name, and a `pie` is a non-metric type that is still a tile on that arm at this head; the title was narrowed from "any widget type" to "a non-metric widget type", which is what is now true. The file's header still describes the metric tile it is about ("must not start rendering them"), and its three CONTROL rows, including the byte-identity of a three-measure `metric` tile, are green at the head. Item 5 holds.

Q1 (the nine unnamed types) and Q2 (the dispatch's item 5 premise that the warning would afterwards fire only for metric-family tiles, measured false). Neither is answered on this card, and that is the ordered outcome: item 3 says a claim that finds them dropping measures "returns an open question" and invents no semantics. Carrying both to objectui#8894 at ACCEPT with `pm:retriage`, rather than holding this PR, is RIGHT: holding would tie the delivery of the spec-named types to a decision triage reserved for itself, and 8894 is the carrier because its plan step C in `5918678067` ("narrow it to the metric family, arm 2 only, after objectui#11261 lands") rests on the premise Q2 measures false. At this head the warning still fires, truly, for a dimensionless multi-measure `pie` / `donut` / `funnel` / `scatter` / `column` / `horizontal-bar` / `radar` / `treemap` / `sankey` (the moved SUBJECT and the nine CONTROL rows pin it), so a narrowing to the metric family would re-silence nine accepted types; Q2 is the same decision as Q1 and belongs beside it. Of the retriage answer's next-claim pins, "a dimensionless `table` shows no warning" is delivered here. The PR must not claim the warning is now metric-only, and it does not: the body says it "no longer fires for the widgets that now render every measure", the changeset does not mention the warning, and no comment in the diff says metric-only.

The out-of-scope observation (a typeless widget with a dimension routes to `bar` through `chartType`'s `??
